intended_object: The natural transformation from the composite "forget to quivers, then take the free (path) category" to the free category functor on reflexive quivers. Its component at a reflexive quiver V is the quotient functor Paths(V) → FreeRefl(V), which identifies each chosen identity arrow with the empty path. This comes from the docstring.
explanation:
The component at a reflexive quiver V is `FreeRefl.quotientFunctor V`. This is the canonical quotient from the path category of the underlying quiver to the free category on V. That free category is defined as the quotient of the path category by the relation that sets each reflexivity arrow equal to the identity.

Naturality says that quotienting and then applying `freeReflMap F` gives the same functor as applying `freeMap F` and then quotienting. Two functors out of a path category agree when they agree on objects and on single arrows, and the proof uses exactly this (`Paths.ext_functor`). The parallel statement is also proved separately as `freeReflMap_naturality`.

The source and target functors are the standard ones on the categories `ReflQuiv` and `Cat`, so the definition is already as general as the notion allows. Nothing else in Mathlib defines this transformation.

It mainly supports the free/forgetful adjunction for reflexive quivers, but it is still a genuine mathematical object: the canonical natural quotient map. So it is faithful.
